Overriding `outDir` from an extended config excludes the wrong
directory. The base's `outDir` lands in the default `exclude` and the
effective one doesnt, so `createFilesMatcher` counts build output as
project source, and the base's directory as build output. Backwards both
ways.

```jsonc
// base.json
{ "compilerOptions": { "outDir": "dist" } }

// tsconfig.json
{ "extends": "./base.json", "compilerOptions": { "outDir": "build" } }
```

```
tsc --showConfig  ->  exclude: ["<dir>/build"],  and ./dist/b.ts listed as a root file
parseTsconfig     ->  exclude: ["dist"],         build/c.ts matches, dist/b.ts doesn't
```

`notes/typescript/v5.9.3/root-file-selection.md` already has the rule
under "Default output exclusions" - the exclusions come from the
*effective* `outDir` and `declarationDir`. But `_parseTsconfig` derives
them per config, so the base derives from `dist` before anything is
merged, and the extending config then sees an `exclude` array already
sat there and skips its own. Thats an inherited default acting like an
explicit one.

Left alone on purpose: an inherited `outDir` still gets excluded at all,
and an explicit `exclude` anywhere in the chain still wins (#89).

---

Separate thing you might want to pick up: the "tsc doesn't add it"
comments in `relative-path.spec.ts` and `merges.spec.ts` are out of
date. On 5.9.3 tsc does add the inherited `outDir`, just as an absolute
path, so those `expectedTsconfig.exclude` overrides are normalising the
form rather than filling in a gap. Ive left them alone.

---------

fix(parse-tsconfig): derive default exclude from the effective outDir (#136)

Overriding `outDir` from an extended config excludes the wrong
directory. The base's `outDir` lands in the default `exclude` and the
effective one doesnt, so `createFilesMatcher` counts build output as
project source, and the base's directory as build output. Backwards both
ways.

```jsonc
// base.json
{ "compilerOptions": { "outDir": "dist" } }

// tsconfig.json
{ "extends": "./base.json", "compilerOptions": { "outDir": "build" } }
```

```
tsc --showConfig  ->  exclude: ["<dir>/build"],  and ./dist/b.ts listed as a root file
parseTsconfig     ->  exclude: ["dist"],         build/c.ts matches, dist/b.ts doesn't
```

`notes/typescript/v5.9.3/root-file-selection.md` already has the rule
under "Default output exclusions" - the exclusions come from the
*effective* `outDir` and `declarationDir`. But `_parseTsconfig` derives
them per config, so the base derives from `dist` before anything is
merged, and the extending config then sees an `exclude` array already
sat there and skips its own. Thats an inherited default acting like an
explicit one.

Left alone on purpose: an inherited `outDir` still gets excluded at all,
and an explicit `exclude` anywhere in the chain still wins (#89).

---

Separate thing you might want to pick up: the "tsc doesn't add it"
comments in `relative-path.spec.ts` and `merges.spec.ts` are out of
date. On 5.9.3 tsc does add the inherited `outDir`, just as an absolute
path, so those `expectedTsconfig.exclude` overrides are normalising the
form rather than filling in a gap. Ive left them alone.
